column2: The wise one should give food to the Brahmins in this order of the planets, according to ability or what is available, honoring them by rule.
A cow, conch, ox, gold, cloth, horse, black cow, iron, goat — these are the fees in order.
Whoever is afflicted by a planet at any time, he should honor that planet with effort. Brahma gave the planets a boon: those honored honor the one who honors.
The rises and falls of kings are under the planets; the existence and non-existence of the world — therefore the planets are most worthy of worship.
Having turned all outward-facing senses inward, one should place the group of senses in the mind and the mind in the Self.
One should place the knower of the field, freed of all states, in Brahman. This is knowledge and meditation; the rest is elaboration of books.
What does not exist for all the world — to say it exists is contradictory; so told, it does not rest in another's heart.
That Brahman is unknowable, like a maiden's face to a woman; the non-yogi does not know it, as one blind from birth a pot.
Seeing a Brahmin with truth and sacrifice the Sun moves from his place: "This one, breaking through my orb, goes to the supreme Brahman."
Fasting vows, bathing, pilgrimage, the fruit of austerity, and the accomplishing of a Brahmin — all that fruit is his.
One syllable is supreme Brahman; breath-control is supreme austerity; there is nothing higher than the Savitri; it is remembered as the supreme purifier.
Women were first enjoyed by the gods, Soma, Gandharvas and Agni; afterward men enjoy them; they are not defiled by anyone.
When a foreign-caste embryo is cast into a woman's womb, the woman remains impure until she releases the thorn;
when the thorn has come out she is purified by menstruation. There is no purification of sinful acts equal to meditation.
Even eating among Shvapakas one is purified by meditation. The Self is the meditator, the mind meditation, Vishnu the object, the fruit is Hari.
An ascetic at an ancestral rite for imperishability purifies the row that purifies. A twice-born who, having ascended to the lifelong-celibate dharma, falls away,
I do not see an atonement by which the suicide could be purified; those who have taken renunciation, and the line of their seed in the wife,
are born as Vidura Chandalas; no doubt here. A vulture dies at a hundred years; and the dog twelve;
a crow twenty years; a boar ten; a tree without flowers and fruit is born covered with thorns;
then burned by forest fire he becomes a stump with his followers; then eight hundred and two years he stays unconscious;
when a thousand years are full he is born a Brahmarakshasa. By a raft he gains liberation, or by uprooting his family.
One should practice yoga alone; no other mantra destroys sin.
Impregnation, the male-engendering rite, then the parting of the hair, birth-rite, naming, first feeding, tonsure,
the sacrament of initiation, the four Vedic vows, the bath, the union with a wife who follows her duty, the five sacrifices:
the sacrifice to gods, to fathers, to men and beings; the Brahma sacrifice; the seven kitchen sacrifices — Ashtakas first;
Parvana rite, Shravani, Agrahayani, Chaitri, Ashvayuji: the seven oblation sacrifices are then remembered;
the fire-installation, Agnihotra, New-moon sacrifice, the animal sacrifice, Chaturmasya, Agrayana, Nirudha-pashubandha;
Sautramani; the seven Soma sacrifices: first Agnishtoma, Atyagnishtoma and Ukthya, Shodashi, Vajapeya,
Atiratra and Aptoryama; and eight qualities of the Self: compassion, forbearance, non-envy, freedom from effort, auspiciousness,
non-meanness, desirelessness, purity — one who has these goes to the supreme. In walking, in intercourse, in urinating, in cleaning teeth,
and at bathing and eating times one should observe silence in six. Giving again, drinking separately, with ghee and fat at night,
cutting teeth and heat one should avoid, seven in barley meal. Having bathed one should not take flowers declared unfit for gods.
One of another gotra, unconnected, who gives the fire to a dead man, and pinda and water, should complete the ten days.
Water, grass, ash, a door and a path — having made a separation by these, there is no fault of the row.
One should give the five breath-oblations with the ring finger and thumb joined.
You, conch, are holy among the holy, the auspicious of auspicious things; always held by Vishnu; therefore grant me peace.
You, Dharma, in the form of a bull, the maker of the world's joy, the support of the eight-formed; therefore grant me peace.
Gold seed in the womb of Hiranyagarbha, of fire, giving endless fruit of merit; therefore grant me peace.
The pair of yellow garments, beloved of Vasudeva — by giving it, Vishnu; therefore grant me peace.
You are Vishnu in the form of a fish, from whom nectar arose, with moon and sun as vehicle always; therefore grant me peace.
Since you, the whole earth, are the cow like Keshava, destroyer of all sin always; therefore grant me peace.
Since iron work is always under you — plows and weapons and the rest; therefore grant me peace.
Since you stand as a limb of all sacrifices, the source of fire always; therefore grant me peace.
In the limbs of cows stand the fourteen worlds; since so, may welfare be mine here and hereafter.
Since the bed of Keshava and Shiva is never empty, may my bed too be never empty, given birth after birth.
As all gods are established in all jewels, so may the gods grant me peace by the gift of jewels.
As other gifts do not deserve a sixteenth part of the gift of land, may peace be mine here from the gift of land.
The planet sacrifice, the ten-thousand oblation, victory in battle by fees; in marriage festivals and sacrifices and in works like installation,
for obtaining all desires, two oblations — a hundred thousand and a crore — are held. In the house region, in a pavilion, for ten thousand, a cubit-sized
pit with girdle and yoni, four priests; or one himself; for a hundred thousand all tenfold;
four cubits or two cubits; one should worship Tarkshya more here. "Sama-sound-headed, you the vehicle of the Supreme,
always remover of objects; therefore grant me peace." Having invited the pit as before one should perform the hundred-thousand oblation;
then one should give the Vasu-stream, give a bed, ornaments and the rest. There too ten and eight priests for the hundred-thousand oblation;
one obtains sons, food, kingdom, victory, enjoyment, liberation and the rest; by fees and fruit therefore the crore-oblator is the destroyer of enemies.
A pit of four or eight cubits, twelve Brahmins; twenty-five or sixteen; on the cloth four at the door;
the crore-oblator gets all desires and goes to Vishnu's world. The oblation with planet-mantras or the Gayatri or Vaishnava,
with those beginning with Jatavedas, Shaiva, Vedic and famed ones; with sesame, barley, ghee one obtains the fruit of the Ashvamedha and the rest.
For hatred and malevolent rites a triangular pit is prescribed; fuel sticks with the left hand joined with hawk-bone and fire,
with red ornaments, loose hair, meditating the enemy's ill: "May the evil-minded be his who hates; hum phat."
One should cut the image with a razor; one should kill the enemy of flour form. Whoever worships one afflicter, having done so goes to heaven.
Meat not prepared for rite, offerings for gods and oblations; of cows and buffaloes, avoiding goats too,
all milks are to be avoided, and their food within ten days. Hare, porcupine, iguana, rhinoceros and tortoise
are declared edible five-nailed; the rest are forbidden. One may eat pathina and rohita fish and sinhatunda;
everything made of barley and wheat and milk-products; Vagasha, Gavacha and others, and food kept with oil.
A Brahmin with Agnihotra fire who acts at will should perform a month's Chandrayana; sitting at the hero's... is beneficial.
Brahmin-killing, drinking liquor, stealing, going to a teacher's wife — they call these great sins, and association with them.
False boasting, informing the king, and false insistence on the teacher's — equal to killing a Brahmin.
Forgetting the Veda, blaming the Veda, false witness, killing a friend, eating forbidden food — six equal to drinking liquor.
Taking a deposit, stealing men, horses and silver, land, diamonds and jewels is remembered as equal to stealing gold.
Casting seed in one's own sisters, virgins, low-caste women, and a friend's or son's wives — they know it equal to the teacher's bed.
Cow-killing, sacrificing for the unfit, adultery, selling oneself, abandoning teacher, mother or father, study and fire and son,
the younger marrying before the elder, and marrying of such, and giving a maiden to them, and officiating for them,
defiling a maiden, usury, breaking a vow, selling a tank, garden, wife and child,
being a Vratya, abandoning kin, teaching for hire, studying from a hired teacher, selling the unsellable,
taking authority in all mines, operating great machines, injury to herbs, living on women, transgressing rites,
felling green trees for fuel, abduction of women, association with slanderers of women,
rites for one's own sake, eating forbidden food, not keeping the sacred fire, theft, not repaying debts,
study of false scripture, bad conduct, addictions, theft of grain, base metals and cattle, drinking liquor and serving women,
killing a woman, Shudra, Vaishya or Kshatriya, atheism — these are minor sins. Hurting a Brahmin, smelling the unsmellable and liquor,
crookedness, and intercourse with a man are remembered as causing loss of caste. Killing dogs, asses, camels, deer, goats and sheep
causes mixing of castes; also of fish, snake and mongoose; accepting wealth from the censured, trade, serving a Shudra
cause unworthiness; speaking untruth, killing worms, insects and birds, eating after drinking liquor,
stealing fruits, fuel and flowers — these bring impurity.
The one who has fallen should, in time, with an ass at a crossroads, worship Nirriti at night by the rule of the kitchen sacrifice;
the wise one, having made the fire by rule, finally with the fuel-verse should offer ghee oblations to Moon, Indra, Jupiter and Fire.
Or wearing an ass's skin he should wander the earth for a year. Having killed an unknown embryo he should perform the Brahmin-killing vow.
A twice-born who has drunk liquor through delusion should drink fire-colored liquor; or fire-colored cow-urine, or water.
A Brahmin thief of gold should approach the king and, proclaiming his deed, say, "Let your honor instruct me."
Taking a pestle the king should strike him once as he comes himself; the thief is purified by the blow, or a Brahmin by austerity alone.
The violator of the teacher's bed, having cut off his own organ and testicles, placing them in his hands, should walk toward the southwest until he falls.
